To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the Lie algebra of vector fields associated with a control system determines whether a given control is real-analytically extendable to a neighborhood of the terminal time of its associated trajectory; (2) the same Lie algebra determines whether the terminal point of a trajectory is regular; and (3) the same Lie-algebra determines whether a given trajectory can be extended to a trajectory that is time-optimal between two given points.
for real-analytically controlled systems, the set of regular controls is open and dense.

for time-optimal control problems, the Lie algebra generated by the control vector fields and their Lie derivatives is the Lie algebra of the vector fields whose flows are the time-optimal flows, and that this Lie algebra is a free Lie algebra of rank equal to the dimension of the control system.
